intervention.description: Corrosion resistance evaluation

evidence_units.mechanism: Electrochemical tests in acidic environment demonstrated high corrosion resistance.
evidence_spans: The obtained samples also exhibited high corrosion resistance under electrochemical tests in H 2 SO 4 solution.
The CrMoNbWV HEA has comparable mechanical and corrosive properties with the WNbMoTaV type HEA, but at the same time has a reduced density: CrMoNbWV—10.55 g/cm 3 , WNbMoTaV—12.42 g/cm 3 .

material.name: NbMoTaWV
material.initial_state: equiatomic composition obtained in prior research

intervention.action: comparison of mechanical properties at elevated temperatures
intervention.description: Comparison with conventional superalloys

structure.description: BCC structure (implied by refractory HEA group)

evidence_units.mechanism: Intrinsic high-temperature stability and solid solution strengthening of refractory elements

outcome.value: hardness up to 11.4 GPa; yield strength (σ 0.2) from 1058 MPa to 1246 MPa

evidence_spans: First high-entropy equiatomic compositions based on refractory elements, such as NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWV, were obtained in prior research [ [4] , [5] ].
It was found that the alloys possess higher mechanical properties at higher temperatures in comparison to conventional superalloys, such as Inconel 718 and Haynes 230 [ [6] ].
It was also determined that the addition of V increases the hardness significantly (up to 11.4 GPa at 1150 °C) [ [7] ] and yield strength σ 0.2 from 1058 MPa to 1246 MPa [ [5] ].
On the other hand, these alloys are brittle at room temperature, leading to significant limitations of their application as structural materials.

evidence_spans: Later, in Reference [ [8] ], it was shown that the addition of Ti to the NbMoTaW alloy might lead to an effective increase of the alloy plasticity up to 11.5% due to the increase of grain boundary cohesion.

intervention.action: formation of coherent BCC and B2 phases

evidence_spans: Thus, for the AlMo 0.5 NbTa 0.5 TiZr alloy, its yield strength is 745 MPa at 1000 °C, and good plasticity is preserved (the height decrease is >50% under compression) [ [12] ].

Volume fractions of Laves phase (Cr,V) 2 (Ta,Nb) and oxide phase Ta 2 VO 6 in this alloy were 7.7% and 6.2%, respectively.
According to the authors, the high mechanical properties were achieved by forming an interstitial solid solution in the matrix and by fine grains (1.24 µm).

intervention.action: mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering
intervention.description: Combined use of MA and SPS for consolidation

intervention.description: High-energy milling to synthesize powder

structure.description: homogeneous structure with light layers 100–300 nm thick enriched with W and Mo
microstructure: light layers with thickness of 100–300 nm
defects: decrease in size of coherent scattering regions

evidence_units.mechanism: diffraction peak broadening caused by decrease in size of coherent scattering regions and increased internal stresses due to intensive mechanical impact
evidence_spans: After 5 h of the MA, the synthesized powder possessed a homogeneous structure.
At the BSE-SEM images, light layers with a thickness of 100–300 nm, enriched with W and Mo can be seen.
Nevertheless, the distribution of the elements within the particle volume was homogeneous in general.
The MA-powder possessed a BCC lattice with a parameter a = 3.146 Å.
The diffraction peak broadening was caused by a decrease in the size of coherent scattering regions and increased internal stresses due to intensive mechanical impact during the MA.

intervention.description: Sintering at 1200 °C

structure.description: BCC solid solution matrix with Laves phases and oxides precipitating
microstructure: fine-crystalline structure without firm grain boundaries
defects: none explicitly stated for this specific unit beyond phase separation

evidence_units.mechanism: separation of elements with small atomic radii (Cr, Fe, V) in the Laves phases and oxides due to sintering
evidence_spans: The XRD results show that the samples after sintering preserve a BCC structure, and its parameter slightly decreases (a = 3.106 Å) due to the separation of elements with small atomic radii (Cr, Fe, V) in the Laves phases and oxides.
At the sintering temperature of 1200 °C, such Laves phases as Cr 2 Nb and (Fe, Cr)Nb, and such oxides mixture as NbVO 4 –VO precipitated.
The samples sintered at 1200 °C had a fine-crystalline structure without firm grain boundaries ( Figure 2 a).

intervention.description: Testing mechanical properties after sintering at 1400 °C

structure.description: BCC-matrix with coarse oxide inclusions

evidence_units.mechanism: coarse oxide inclusions act as crack initiation sources causing fractures in the BCC-matrix
evidence_spans: The volume fraction of the Laves phases decreased in the sample sintered at 1400 °C.
However, the oxide particle size significantly increases, as shown in Figure 2 .
The coarse inclusions can act as a crack initiation source and cause fractures in the BCC-matrix that leads to a decrease of the HEA plasticity.

intervention.description: Polarization tests in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4

structure.description: BCC matrix with varying phase fractions based on temperature

evidence_units.mechanism: increase of the SPS temperature provided a positive shift of the E OCP and a decrease of i corr
evidence_spans: Figure 6 represents the polarization curves for the CrMoNbWV HEA SPS-samples in the 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 used as electrolytes at room temperature.
The values of E OCP and i corr are shown in Table 4 .
All three samples exhibited good resistance to general corrosion in the sulfuric acid solution, i corr reach 2.81×, 0.20, and 0.88 µA/cm 2 , respectively.

The increase of the SPS temperature provided a positive shift of the E OCP and a decrease of i corr , leading to the good corrosion resistance of the SPS samples obtained at 1300–1400 °C, in H 2 SO 4 solution.

intervention.description: Tafel polarization curves on carburized layer

structure.description: carburized layer with HEA carbides

evidence_units.mechanism: SPS temperature increase resulted in decrease of i corr and shift of E OCP to higher positive values
evidence_spans: Figure 8 represents the Tafel polarization curves obtained for the carburized layer of the HEA SPS-samples.
The electrolyte was the 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 solution at room temperature.
The SPS temperature increase resulted in a decrease of i corr , where the values were 0.91, 0.66, and 0.21 µA/cm 2 .
On the contrary, the E OCP shifted to higher positive values from 100 to 276 mV, respectively.
The results showed that the chemical stability of the carburized layer increases with increasing sintering temperature.

candidate.mechanism: Temperature increase to 1400 °C led to grain coarsening and decomposition of the solid solution phase, reducing Laves phase content while precipitating at grain boundaries.
evidence_spans: In this study, bulk samples of a CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy (HEA) were obtained for the first time by spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed (MA) powders at 1200 °C, 1300 °C, and 1400 °C.
The MA powders' phase composition was found to be represented by body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solution.
The solid solution partially decomposed to Laves phases under the sintering, such as Cr 2 Nb and (Fe, Cr)Nb, and NbVO 4 -VO oxides mixture.
The temperature increase to 1400 °C led to a grain coarsening of the BCC phase and decreased the Laves phase content accompanied by precipitation at the grain boundaries.
The sintered samples showed high hardness and compressive strength (2700–2800 MPa) at room temperature.
The wear tests demonstrated excellent results in comparison to conventional wear-resistant composites.

evidence_spans: Prior research shows the mechanical properties of the refractory NbMoWVTa [ [5] ] and NbMoWVTaTi [ [27] ] HEAs obtained by arc melting, where the compressive strength of the alloys are 1270 and 2000 MPa, respectively.
In this paper, the CrMoNbWV HEA, obtained by SPS of the MA-powder, has a structure with equiaxial grains with a size of less than 15 µm.

The high strength values of samples obtained by powder metallurgy methods can be explained by the influence of the following hardening mechanisms: (1) grain boundary hardening described by Hall–Petch relationship; (2) solid solution hardening due to strong lattice strains caused by substitutional elements; (3) solid solution hardening by interstitial elements; (4) Laves phases and oxides precipitations.
The Laves phases and oxides, formed under the SPS, are dispersed in the matrix and serve as barriers for dislocation motions.
The sintered samples exhibit the compressive strength of 2700–2870 MPa.
The samples' low plasticity is caused by the high volume fraction of the Laves phases localized at the grain boundaries.
